title: KV-prefix caching RFC — architecture review notes
content:
Architecture review notes — KV-prefix caching RFC (session 2025-02-13)

Attendees: Maya Chen (facilitator), Arjun Patel, Lena Novak, Diego Morales, Sasha Ivanov, Priya Raman (observer)
Duration: 60m
Context / purpose:
- Review the draft RFC proposing a lightweight per-model KV-prefix cache that stores decoded key-value cache segments for common prefixes across requests. Goal: reduce redundant decompression/deserialize work and lower p99 token latency for short-turn conversations and few-shot prompts while preserving memory isolation between tenants.
- Tradeoffs being considered: memory amplification vs CPU savings; invalidation semantics; cross-model compatibility; integration surface with existing batching and KV eviction.

Summary of proposed design (short):
1) Per-model in-memory cache keyed by (model-id, prefix-hash, sequence-length-bucket). Values: serialized token-KV chunk (gzipped) + metadata (last-access, seq-start, seq-end).
2) Cache population happens asynchronously after responses are produced by inference worker — worker emits 'kv-diff' event with prefix-hash and compressed-kv which is merged into the model cache by cache-manager process.
3) Read path: prior to decoding tokens for a new request, router checks cache for matching prefix-hash and sequence-length bucket; if hit, RPC returns preloaded KV to worker so decoding can start from warmed state.
4) Eviction: LRU with adaptive weights (size, age, hit-rate). Memory cap per-model set by tenant plan (hosted/dedicated tiers).
5) Isolation: cache entries tagged with tenancy metadata; cross-tenant sharing forbidden. Options for cross-model sharing (same weights/head config) deferred for follow-up RFC.

Key decisions we discussed:
- Copy vs share: we will copy KV into worker process memory on cache-hit rather than try to memory-map shared pages to avoid complexity with worker lifecycle and GC. Tradeoff: CPU copy cost but simpler lifecycle and safer for dedicated workloads. (Decision: copy, for now)
- Compression format: zstd level 3 chosen as default for acceptable decompression latency on A100/RTX platforms; allow per-deployment override. (Decision: zstd-3)
- Sequence-length bucketing: use coarse buckets: 1-32, 33-128, 129-512, 513-2048 to reduce fragmentation. (Decision: coarse buckets; revisit after telemetry)
- Invalidation strategy: on model version rollout, invalidate model-id namespace. For prompt-specific invalidation (user-supplied dynamic context), the router must include prompt-hash; we will not attempt partial KV patching across prompt changes. (Decision: namespace-based invalidation + prefix-hash keyed for per-request variation)

Open technical risks and notes:
- Memory amplification: storing decoded KV for many prefixes could increase host memory by ~30-60% under synthetic traces. Need to run a 7d simulation with real traffic slices (small, medium, large customers) to estimate realistic amplification and set sane defaults. (Action: Diego)
- Consistency between batching and cache-hits: if a request is batched with others, preloading KV must occur before batch assembly; race condition possible when one request in batch has cache-hit and others need warmup. We discussed two approaches: 1) always assemble batch from warmed workers (may increase latency for cold requests), 2) allow mixed batch but ensure the runtime accepts per-request KV offsets. Option 2 requires more changes to the batch serialization layer. (Action: Arjun + Lena to prototype approach #2 with minimal API changes)
- Telemetry surface: must record cache-hit/miss, size-on-disk, decompression time, copy time, and per-tenant memory footprint. Add new metrics prefixed with serving.kvcache.* and integrate into console dashboards. (Action: Sasha)

Security & multi-tenancy concerns:
- Even though prefix-hash is derived from input prefixes, risk of information leakage through side-channels if a tenant can probe cache hits. Mitigations: per-tenant namespaces, rate-limiting on cache-populate events, and auditing of cache access. Need security review. (Action: schedule with Security team; owner Maya)

Performance expectations and SLO impact:
- Target p99 token latency reduction: 10–25% for short-turn flows at low sequence lengths (<=128). Cost: small CPU overhead for copy + zstd decompress (~0.5–1.2ms on typical inference worker).
- Should not increase p50; fallback path on miss is identical to existing decode path. Must ensure miss path steady-state is unchanged.

Implementation plan / milestones (rough):
- Week 0–1: Prototype: cache-manager process + simple in-memory map, worker-side integration for copy-on-hit. Add feature flag. (Owners: Arjun, Diego)
- Week 2: Internal perf tests using replayed traffic; run memory amplification simulation. (Owners: Diego, Sasha)
- Week 3: Extend eviction policy and per-tenant caps; add metrics. (Owners: Lena, Sasha)
- Week 4: Canary on dedicated pool with opt-in flag; collect telemetry. (Owners: Arjun)
- Week 6: Rollout to hosted with conservative caps, monitor. (Owners: eng-serving-runtime leads)

Action items (owner — due):
- Diego: run 7-day memory amplification simulation and produce a spreadsheet with per-tenant projected memory delta, and recommend defaults for per-model caps — due 2025-02-21.
- Arjun & Lena: prototype batch-aware read path that allows per-request KV offsets without blocking batch assembly; open prototype PR and perf microbench by 2025-02-20.
- Sasha: instrument serving.kvcache.* metrics, add Grafana dashboard skeleton, and list of alerts for unexpected growth — due 2025-02-18.
- Maya: schedule security review with Security & Privacy (include threat model), attach findings to RFC — due 2025-02-19.
- Priya (observer): capture UX notes for operator controls (console toggles, caps UI) and share in product channel — due 2025-02-17.

Unresolved questions (for follow-up RFCs):
- Cross-model sharing: under what conditions (same architecture, identical kv layout) can we safely reuse KV across model variants? Need compatibility matrix and correctness tests.
- On-disk cache option: evaluate a local SSD-backed cache for very large KV entries to reduce memory pressure but with higher latencies — tradeoffs to be explored.
- Auto-tuning eviction weights based on workload signals (burstiness, reuse rate) vs static heuristics.

Notes from discussion (raw fragments):
- Sasha: "If we can shave 1ms off p99 for chat, that's a huge UX win even if memory goes up a bit for dedicated tenants."
- Diego: "Simulator with sampled traces should show whether 30% mem increase is pessimistic — our synthetic was worst-case."
- Arjun: "Batch layer changes are hairy but possible — we should prototype with an opt-in switch. If we can keep copy cost sub-ms it's fine."
- Lena: "We should ensure the dashboard exposes 'hot prefixes' per tenant so customers can see what is being cached and why."

Decision log (to be appended to RFC):
- Copy-on-hit chosen over shared memory mapping (rationale: simpler lifecycle, predictable for dedicated).
- zstd-3 as default compression format.
- Coarse sequence-length buckets chosen.
- Invalidation via model-version namespace + prefix-hash.

Next steps:
- Update RFC with decisions above and attach prototype plan (Arjun will update RFC draft by 2025-02-15).
- Hold a short demo of prototype during next weekly runtime sync once Arjun/Lena have a working branch (target demo week of 2025-02-24).

Appendix (quick checklist for PR reviewers):
- Does the PR add serving.kvcache.* metrics? (yes/no)
- Is there feature-flag gating for enabling cache at runtime? (yes/no)
- Are per-tenant caps configurable via config + console UI? (yes/no)
- Does the PR include unit tests for invalidation semantics? (yes/no)
- Is there a memory safety review (valgrind/asan/cgroup tests) documented? (yes/no)

End of notes.

Document version: draft-1 (internal review).
